question.problem:
Consider the matrix $A$ for which ${\lambda }_{1}=5,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=-5$ are eigenvalues, and

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

are the respective eigenvectors. What are the values of $a,b,c$ given that

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}a & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & b \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & c\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}a & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & b \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}?
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=5,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=-5,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal: 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=5,$

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ and

- the $3$rd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{3}=-5.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}.
$$

In conclusion, we get $a=-2,$ $b=0,$ and $c=-5.$
